key_insight: LACUNA introduces a testbed to measure how precisely unlearning methods localize and remove knowledge inside an LLM, not just whether the output changes. It helps reveal when apparent unlearning may still leave memorized information in the model’s parameters.
problem_solved: Existing unlearning benchmarks mostly check outputs, which can miss whether sensitive information is truly erased from the model. This paper addresses the need for a way to evaluate localization precision in post hoc LLM unlearning, especially for PII removal.
method: Defines a testbed for evaluating localization precision in LLM unlearning.
Focuses on the common localize-first, unlearn-second pipeline used by state-of-the-art methods.
Assesses whether targeted parameters are actually responsible for the memorized knowledge, rather than only observing output-level forgetting.
impact: This matters because practitioners need stronger guarantees that sensitive training data is genuinely removed, not merely hidden. Better evaluation can make unlearning methods more trustworthy for privacy, compliance, and safe deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing locate → unlearn → evaluate
Before/after model-memory illustration highlighting residual knowledge
Comparison chart of output-level vs parameter-level evaluation
Icon set for privacy, parameters, and forgetting
paper_title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
paper_authors: Matteo Boglioni, Thibault Rousset, Siva Reddy, Marius Mosbach, Verna Dankers
